publicPrompt:
Create a NEW ORIGINAL Catch! Teenieping who belongs convincingly in the supplied cast. The source photo is a character-design seed, not a real person to miniaturize.

IMAGE 1: blue Teenieping — reference for the head/face, tiny body and smooth render finish ONLY. Discard its tail, cap, side hair shape and any other character-specific appendages.
IMAGE 2: simple magenta Teenieping — reference for colored creature body, tiny anatomy, sculpted fantasy hair.
IMAGE 3: red dress Teenieping — reference for a symbolic costume and recognizable theme on the same tiny creature.
IMAGE 4: source photograph — read its hairstyle SHAPE, eyewear, clothing category, main garment colors, pose/action, meaningful objects and setting.

MANDATORY SOURCE FACTS — THESE OVERRIDE FANTASY RECOLORING:
Fantasy recoloring applies ONLY to hair, irises and pale creature body tint. It does NOT authorize recoloring the source clothes, glasses or held objects.
Before designing, read and lock each person's actual upper garment hue, lower garment hue, eyewear frame shape/color, hairstyle SHAPE, seated/standing pose and held object. Preserve these as separate source facts, not inferred from gender, background or activity.
Keep each garment's original hue category even in a magical costume. You may simplify materials and vary lightness slightly, but blue clothes remain blue, beige remain beige, green remain green, yellow remain yellow. Do not replace a garment with the theme color, skin color, prop color or a reference character's costume color. Tiny motif/trim accents cannot replace the dominant garment area.
A skirt/dress is ONE smooth continuous shell with ONE unbroken hem and original dominant hue. No crotch split or separate leg tubes. A trouser/shorts source has TWO distinctly CLOTHED little leg openings in its original garment hue, with a visible waistband/hem boundary and split between them. Do not replace trousers with bare white creature body or add an over-skirt. Keep original sleeve coverage. Glasses require both full frames and bridge, matching source shape/color, in front of the eyes.
Use only a head, torso, two arms and two legs for each human source. Absolutely NO TAIL, wings, animal ears, side fins, back spikes, extra limbs or reference-creature appendages. In Image 1, the tail is NOT transferable. Preserve short hair as a compact short hair cap; do not copy reference side pigtails/long lobes onto a short-haired source.
Preserve posture and support: a seated source stays seated with the body resting on its source seat, not standing or floating. A standing source remains standing. Adapt scale and tiny limb angles, not the meaningful pose.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE:
Translate the person into a small magical BEING with an activity-based power/personality, like the real Teenieping cast. Do not reproduce realistic human hair colors, skin materials or miniature everyday clothes. Identity comes from recognizable hair silhouette, glasses/accessories, major clothing colors and the source action. Unlike previous literal photo transforms, HAIR COLOR MAY CHANGE to a saturated thematic fantasy hue.

CHOOSE A COHERENT NEW DESIGN FROM THE SOURCE:
Infer ONE main motif from the meaningful activity/object. Build a compact vivid fantasy palette from that motif and the source props, while keeping the source upper/lower clothing colors recognizable. Use a saturated theme color for the smooth hair and a harmonious iris color; a much paler contrasting tint for the face/body. Plant-care may suggest mint/emerald, drawing may suggest a vivid crayon color, reading may suggest ink blue or a bright book-cover color. These are conditional options, not a global green character rule. Do not make every subject pink, or turn every input into the same princess.
Keep short/long hairstyle shape, bangs and ponytail count from the photo, but turn them into a few oversized bold curved candy-like shapes. Invent one small simple motif jewel integrated into the hair design and repeat that motif once as a small chest emblem. No unrelated crowns, ribbons, hearts, wings or giant accessories.
If the source wears glasses, visibly include BOTH complete matching-shape/color frames and bridge in front of the eyes with clear lenses. If no glasses, add none. Source skirt/dress MUST stay one smooth continuous skirt shell; source trousers/shorts MUST stay two distinct small leg openings. No skirt on trouser inputs. Retain source presentation; boys must not automatically become princesses.

EXACT TEENIEPING ANATOMY AND FINISH:
Use Image 1's ACTUAL wide rounded-square face plate, eye spacing, low short chin, tiny flat dot nose and almost invisible neck. The head is not a spherical human baby's head. Eyes are clean ovals, very dark pupils, luminous colored lower iris rim and one large white circular highlight plus one tiny dot each. Tiny simple mouth with a little visible red tongue when smiling. Minimal source-appropriate lashes.
Head/hair is roughly two thirds of height. Body is a tiny smooth teardrop, very short stub/flipper arms with mitten tips, tiny pointed feet continuous with body. No human ears, wrists, articulated fingers, muscular calves or realistic separate shoes.
HAIR IS ONE SMOOTH OPAQUE SCULPTURE with a few broad lobes, saturated color, broad soft highlights. Absolutely no strand lines, fur, fiber, grooves, grain, realistic hair reflection or clay texture.
CLOTHING IS A TINY MAGIC COSTUME, not tiny retail clothes. Translate source cardigan/hoodie/shirt silhouette into one or two simple smooth color shapes with a plain edge. Keep source sleeve coverage and top/bottom color distinction. A skirt becomes one small smooth bell/A-line shell; trousers become two small smooth leg openings. No knit, denim, stitching, belt loops, zipper, laces, fabric folds or oversized clothes. Use only a simple color tip for footwear.
The finish must match the supplied original CGI character art: smooth polished opaque colored surfaces, broad clean shading, soft even studio-like animation illumination. No product-photography doll lighting, golden cinematic backlight, photographic materials or human-portrait aesthetic.

SCENE:
Stage the source's meaningful action with adapted tiny limbs, source gaze direction and recognizable main prop relationships. Keep EACH hand's separate role and original object-contact count: two-handed holding stays two-handed; a drawing hand draws while the other supports paper. Scale props for visible contact.
Use a clear, boldly simplified 3D TV-cartoon version of the source setting, with broad smooth shapes and flat material colors, NOT the photographic background. All props/foliage/furniture use the same clean character-world geometry. Show a large readable protagonist with full body and feet where possible, medium composition, limited blur. Source people count only, no added characters, words, grid, logo, labels, watermark, border or comparison panels.

FINAL CHECK AGAINST THE SOURCE PHOTO:
Verify both glasses frames/bridge; each upper and lower garment's original hue; continuous skirt versus TWO visibly clothed trouser legs; compact/long/tied hair silhouette; original seated/standing support; each hand-object contact; and ABSOLUTELY NO TAIL or extra anatomy. Remove any reference-only tail or other copied feature. Keep the saturated fantasy hair and activity insignia while preserving all these source facts.
